title: Observability for LLM Inference on Kubernetes
tldr: With frontier APIs you only see the client side, but self-hosting on Kubernetes lets you observe every layer from the GPU up to the user response. The speakers instrument an OCR app on KServe, vLLM and llm-d with OpenTelemetry and correlate metrics, traces and logs in Grafana to find wasted tokens and misleading GPU utilization.

key_points.text: Inference has a prefill stage and an iterative decode stage, which give the two core metrics: time to first token and time per output token.
With frontier model APIs you can instrument your app with OpenTelemetry GenAI traces, but not model internals, GPU use or KV cache, and provider features change over time.
Provider-reported TTFT differed from client-measured TTFT because of network hops and client processing.
With a local model capped at four parallel requests, extra requests show up as deferred, which is what a slow chat response feels like.
Demo app: passport OCR using an open-weights Qwen 9B vision model on one Kubernetes GPU node with KServe and vLLM, llm-d routing and Envoy Gateway in front.
Signals span five layers: application, routing (scheduler latency), inference server (TTFT, KV cache), hardware (GPU) and Kubernetes (vLLM startup, scheduling, unhealthy events).
DCGM dashboards show a GPU at 100% utilization while KV cache was only 20% busy, so GPU utilization alone misleads.
OpenTelemetry traces cover model loading in vLLM and full request paths, including a failed span whose cause was an empty model response.
The OpenTelemetry Collector sends signals to Prometheus, Tempo and Loki; correlation uses exemplars, trace ID queries, span metrics and the GenAI semantic conventions.
Findings: thinking mode wasted tokens for the vision model without improving answers, and batching many requests at once saved cost and energy.

numbers.text: OpenAI test script: 5 requests, about 100 tokens per second throughput.
Provider dashboard showed 600 ms TTFT while the client measured about 1.5 seconds.
Local model configured for 4 parallel requests; GPU utilization near 90% under load.
GPU at 100% utilization with KV cache only 20% busy.
Compared 1 request versus 24 requests at once for cost and energy.

open_gaps.text: Hosted frontier APIs hide model internals, GPU and KV cache behavior from users.
On neo-cloud GPUs you do not own the hardware, so power and energy data is not accurate.
The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions are still in development.

opportunities.text: Build a GPU dashboard that shows KV cache usage next to DCGM utilization so busy-but-idle GPUs stand out.
Use OpenTelemetry exemplars and span metrics to jump from a latency spike to the trace and the endpoint picker logs.
Measure token use with thinking mode on and off for your workload before enabling it.
Compare client-measured TTFT with provider-reported TTFT to size network and client overhead.
